authors: Timney B, Keil K
title: Visual acuity in the horse
why: Primary measurement of horse grating acuity, the only number a horse row can state at grade m.

authors: ENTSU S, Dohi H, Yamada A
title: Visual acuity of cattle determined by the method of discrimination learning
why: Behavioural acuity of cattle; no measured figure for Bos taurus is in hand.

authors: Hebel R
title: Distribution of retinal ganglion cells in five mammalian species (pig, sheep, ox, horse, dog)
why: Ganglion-cell maps of pig, sheep, ox, horse and dog in one paper: streak and area centralis for the species a deer view is lent to.

authors: Hutson G
title: Visual field, restricted vision and sheep movement in laneways
why: Measured visual field of sheep, the nearest number for the field of view of the commonest farm ruminant.

authors: Birgersson J, Alm U, Forkman B
title: Colour vision in fallow deer: a behavioural study
why: Behavioural colour discrimination in fallow deer; checks that a two-cone ungulate in the Cervidae chooses by colour as the deer view assumes.

authors: Macuda T, Timney B
title: Luminance and chromatic discrimination in the horse (Equus caballus)
why: Horse luminance and chromatic discrimination: which colours a horse separates.

authors: Banks MS, Sprague WW, et al.
title: Why do animal eyes have pupils of different shapes?
why: Its supplementary table gives pupil shape for each of more than 200 species; it would settle lion, tiger, cougar, bobcat, coyote, grey fox and goat in one table.
get: open access (Science Advances); the supplementary table is the item

authors: Jacobs GH, Birch DG, Blakeslee B
title: Visual acuity and spatial contrast sensitivity in tree squirrels
why: Grating acuity and contrast sensitivity of tree squirrels (Sciurus); the only acuity figure in hand is a 14 cpd guess from a ground squirrel.

authors: Abdel KM
title: Topographie und Verteilung retinaler Zellen bei Caniden
why: Open thesis (Vienna) mapping cone topography in wild canids and domestic dogs; may cover wolf, fox and jackal streaks that the dog view lends to coyotes.

authors: Sugnaseelan S, Prescott NB, Broom DM, Wathes C, et al.
title: Visual discrimination learning and spatial acuity in sheep
why: Spatial acuity of sheep by discrimination learning.

authors: Tanaka T, Hashimoto A, Tanida H, Yoshimoto T
title: Studies on the visual acuity of sheep using shape discrimination learning
why: Sheep acuity by shape discrimination; second measurement to compare with the 2013 figure.

authors: Smith BL, Skotko DJ, Owen W, McDaniel RJ
title: Color Vision in the White-Tailed Deer
why: Behavioural colour tests in white-tailed deer, the species the rows were written for.

authors: Hanggi EB, Ingersoll JF, Waggoner T
title: Color vision in horses (Equus caballus): Deficiencies identified using a pseudoisochromatic plate test.
why: Horse colour deficiencies on a plate test: which hues are confused.

authors: Harman AM, MOORE S, Hoskins R, Keller PR
title: Horse vision and an explanation for the visual behaviour originally explained by the ‘ramp retina’
why: Tests the ramp-retina claim about horse head posture; decides whether a horse row may say the horse tilts its sight.

authors: Sivak JG, Allen D
title: An evaluation of the “ramp” retina of the horse eye
why: Optical test of the horse ramp retina; companion to Harman 1999.

authors: Shinozaki A, Takagi S, Hosaka YZ, Uehara M
title: The fibrous tapetum of the horse eye
why: Structure and extent of the horse tapetum fibrosum.

authors: François J, Wouters L, Victoria-Troncoso V, Rouck AD, et al.
title: Morphometric and Electrophysiologic Study of the Photoreceptors in the Horse
why: Photoreceptor counts across the horse retina (cones, rods, density by region).

authors: Johnson GL
title: I. Contributions to the comparative anatomy of the mammalian eye, chiefly based on ophthalmoscopic examination
journal: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London Series B Containing Papers of a Biological Character
why: Ophthalmoscopic survey of fundus colour and tapetum type across many mammals; decides which lent species have a tapetum (rodents, camelids, felids, canids).

authors: Timney B, Macuda T
title: Vision and hearing in horses
journal: Journal of the American Veterinary Medical Association
why: Veterinary review of horse vision and hearing; collects field, acuity, colour and dim-light figures in one place.

authors: Szél Á, Röhlich P
title: Two cone types of rat retina detected by anti-visual pigment antibodies
why: Antibody study of rat cone types; checks whether the rat has one or two kinds of colour-sensing cell, which decides if rats may borrow the squirrel colour row.

authors: Anderson DH, Jacobs GH
title: Color vision and visual sensitivity in the California ground squirrel (Citellus beecheyi)
why: Colour vision and sensitivity in the California ground squirrel; behavioural basis for the squirrel colour row.

authors: Evans KE, McGreevy PD
title: The Distribution of Ganglion Cells in the Equine Retina and its Relationship to Skull Morphology
why: Full text gives the ganglion-cell densities behind the horse streak and how much they vary between breeds.

authors: Shinozaki A, Hosaka YZ, Imagawa T, Uehara M
title: Topography of ganglion cells and photoreceptors in the sheep retina
why: Full text of the sheep retina topography (abstract read): cone and rod maps and tapetum extent.
